study_identification_part.si4_title: Adjustment of Regional Cortical Thickness Measures for Global Cortical Thickness Obscures Deficits Across the Schizophrenia Spectrum: A Cautionary Note About Normative Modeling of Brain Imaging Data

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its research hypotheses/questions and describes the purpose of examining normative modeling approaches. The authors hypothesize that (1) covarying for global thickness would attenuate or eliminate patient group regional thickness abnormalities; (2) this would be especially true when there are patient group abnormalities in global thickness and when global and regional thickness are highly correlated; and (3) adjustment for ICV would not have the same detrimental effect. The purpose is to demonstrate that global thickness adjustment in normative modeling leads to erroneous conclusions about thickness abnormalities in psychiatric disorders. Both criteria are met: research hypotheses are provided, and the purpose of applying normative modeling (critique of global covariation approach) is described.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We hypothesized that 1) covarying for global thickness would attenuate or eliminate patient group regional thickness abnormalities; 2) this would be especially true when there are patient group abnormalities in global thickness and when global and regional thickness are highly correlated; and 3) adjustment for ICV would not have the same detrimental effect. | To provide empirical support for the above arguments, we examined regional thickness profiles from 2 archival magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies.

(1) The meaning and direction of deviation scores ARE explained - z-scores represent deviation from HC-expected values for a person of same age, gender, and site. Negative z-scores indicate thinner cortex relative to healthy expectations. (2) Quantitative thresholds for categorizing deviations are NOT reported - the study does not define 'extreme' or 'atypical' thresholds (e.g., |Z| > 1.96 or percentile cutoffs). The analysis focuses on group mean differences rather than individual classification. Limitations of global adjustment interpretation are addressed. Two of three criteria are met.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: Adjusted z scores represent each participant's deviation from the value expected for an HC of the same age, gender, and site. | Regional widespread schizophrenia spectrum group differences (large effect sizes) were eliminated with global thickness adjustment, even though adjustments were modeled using only HC data. In fact, global thickness adjustment distorted schizophrenia spectrum group profiles so much that, paradoxically, adjusted z scores for some ROIs were rendered abnormally thicker. | We argue that future studies that examine regional thickness in psychiatric disorders abandon statistical global thickness adjustment and that publicly disseminated tools include the option to omit global thickness adjustment. | These analytical methods are important to clarify because conclusions drawn from these studies inform our understanding of disease pathophysiology and the advancement of prognostic biomarkers.
